newsitem.title: CANADA: AWP sees more feed wheat, malt barley than average.
newsitem.headline: AWP sees more feed wheat, malt barley than average.

text.p: Alberta Wheat Pool on Friday issued its estimate of crop quality as of Oct 25 compared with the 10-year average.

Thirty percent of hard red spring wheat should grade No1 Canada Western Red Spring compared with 29 percent average. Eight percent should grade No2 CWRS compared to 24 percent. Thirty nine percent should grade No3 CWRS versus 30 percent and 23 percent should grade feed wheat compared to 16 percent.
Eighteen percent of barley should grade as malt compared to 13 percent, 67 percent as No1 Canada Western compared to 71 percent and 15 percent as No2 CW compared to 16 percent.
Eighty-six percent of canola should grade as No1 Canada compared to 72 percent, 11 percent as No2 C compared to 17 percent and two percent as No3 C compared to 7 percent.
AWP said it would issue its last crop report Nov 1. AWP's 1996 crop quality survey will be issued at a yet-to-be-determined date after November 1.
